claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a child named Alex who is 8 years old. I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'll help you determine if you're eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me first review the eligibility rules to ensure I give you accurate guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. Now I have the eligibility rules, I need to ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! And just to confirm:

**Does Alex live with you in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand more about the situation.

**Could you tell me who Alex is currently living with, and do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is in the process of being adopted by me, but they haven't come to live with me yet. I do contribute towards their upkeep though - I help with things like clothes and other essentials.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is helpful information about the adoption process and your contributions.

**Has Alex actually come to live with you yet, even if the adoption process isn't complete? Or are they still living elsewhere while the adoption is being finalized?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't come to live with me yet. They're still living elsewhere while we're going through the adoption process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I need to understand a bit more about your contributions to assess your eligibility properly.

**Can you tell me approximately how much you contribute towards Alex's upkeep? Specifically, is it at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be (which is currently around £25 per week for the eldest or only child, or about £102-108 per month)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute about £30 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more important question:

**Is the local council currently paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while they are living elsewhere?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

## Summary

Based on your circumstances, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

Here's why: According to the official government guidance, you can claim Child Benefit for a child you're adopting **as soon as they come to live with you** - you don't have to wait until the adoption process is complete. However, since Alex hasn't come to live with you yet, your situation falls into a special category.

The guidance specifically states: *"You might be able to get Child Benefit for a period before the adoption - contact the Child Benefit Office to find out."*

While you are contributing financially towards Alex's upkeep (£30 per week, which exceeds the typical Child Benefit amount), and the local council isn't paying towards their accommodation or maintenance, the specific rules for claiming Child Benefit during the pre-placement phase of an adoption require direct assessment by HMRC.

**What you should do:** Contact the Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific adoption circumstances. They will be able to assess whether you can claim Child Benefit for the period before Alex comes to live with you, and advise you on when and how to make your claim.

Once Alex does come to live with you, you will definitely be able to claim Child Benefit for them (even while the adoption process is still being completed).
